descriptionChirho: The practice or act of fasting, abstaining from food as a spiritual discipline, appearing in both singular and plural forms referring to the general religious practice. Eng 'fasting/fastings,' spa 'ayuno/ayunos,' hin 'upvas/upvason,' arb 'siyam/aswam,' kor 'geumsik,' swa 'kufunga.' The plural and singular dative forms describe the ongoing practice of fasting as part of devotional life (2 Cor 6:5, 11:27; Luke 2:37).

The specific calendrical fast referring to Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement, used as a seasonal time marker in Acts 27:9. Distinguished by capitalization and the definite article in translations: eng 'the Fast,' spa 'el Ayuno,' hin 'upvas,' arb 'al-sawm,' swa 'Saumu.' This is not general fasting practice but a proper designation for the most solemn fast day in the Jewish liturgical calendar, used here to indicate dangerous sailing season in the Mediterranean.
